let's pick up the next chunk of this work!

  Handover — Data-API auth-context slice (next)

  Where we got to

  PR #1367 (cor-389-control-plane-context-aware, draft) makes the control plane follow the active auth context:
  - org/repo/project/grant + auth status dial the active context's login server, with silent JWT refresh (auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget → NewRefreshingLoginProvider). ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL
  is a fallback, not an override.
  - Stale cross-core warning removed; review comments addressed.
  - Design doc: docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md — the "one core (login server) + resource servers" model. Read this first.

  Already done elsewhere: git clusters are context-aware via internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery (/.well-known/entire-cluster.json → core_urls → pick context). That's the template.

  The goal of the next slice

  Make ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity (no ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL) auto-pick the right login context. Affected commands: activity, search, trail, dispatch.

  Two parts

  1. Server — ~/src/entirehq/entire.io (you own this)

  Add GET /.well-known/entire-api.json, unauthenticated, advertising trust roots:
  { "issuer": "https://us.auth.partial.to",
    "trusted_issuers": ["https://us.auth.partial.to", "https://eu.auth.partial.to"],
    "audience": "entire-web-api",
    "jwks_uri": "https://us.auth.partial.to/.well-known/jwks.json" }
  - Source straight from existing config in api/src/env.ts: ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL (issuer), ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS (trusted_issuers), ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE (audience). The server
  already knows all this — it just doesn't publish it.
  - Mount in api/src/app.ts route table; no auth middleware.
  - Reference implementation: entiredb's ~/src/entirehq/entiredb/server/cluster_discovery.go.
  - partial.to is the staging deploy of the same code, so it comes for free.

  2. Client — this repo

  - Generalize internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery: make the well-known path + response shape pluggable so it serves both entire-cluster.json (core_urls) and entire-api.json ({issuer,
  trusted_issuers, audience, jwks_uri}). Reuse its selectContext and the discovery/ cache.
    - Selection rule differs from the control plane: here a host is being matched, so use cluster semantics — active context wins only if eligible (its CoreURL ∈ trusted_issuers), else
  sole-eligible, else error. (Control plane was "active always wins" because it had no host to match.) This is exactly the entire.io-active-but-hitting-partial.to case you raised earlier.
  - Wire into the seams (audit: ~11 call sites, 3 constructors):
    - cmd/entire/cli/api_client.go → NewAuthenticatedAPIClient (activity, trail; search token resolution)
    - cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/cloud.go → NewCloudClient
    - cmd/entire/cli/search/search.go → Search (also honors ENTIRE_SEARCH_URL, falls back to API base)
  - Fallback: if entire-api.json 404s (old deployment / not rolled out), fall back to today's static resolution so nothing breaks pre-deploy.

  ⚠️  The one real unknown — audience vs host

  NewAuthenticatedAPIClient today does auth.TokenForResource(ctx, api.OriginOnly(dataURL)) — it exchanges for an audience derived from the data host origin. But entire.io validates aud
  against ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE = entire-web-api (an opaque string, not the host). So:
  - First, figure out how this works today (does the core token already cover it via same-origin shortcut? is ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE currently set to the host URL?).
  - Then: the well-known advertises audience, and the CLI must exchange for that opaque audience, not the host origin. Verify auth-go tokenmanager supports an explicit/opaque audience (vs
  origin-derived TokenRequest.Resource). If it doesn't, that's the first thing to add (a TokenForAudience-style path). This is the crux of the slice — settle it before wiring call sites.

  Pointers

  - Design + deferred notes: docs/architecture/upstream-host-resolution.md
  - Client discovery to generalize: internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery/{discovery,resolve}.go, cache in internal/entireclient/discovery/
  - Token exchange: cmd/entire/cli/auth/exchange.go (TokenForResource, TokenRequest), auth-go tokenmanager
  - Two-surface caution (never touch legacy ent_ PATs): memory auth-token-surfaces
  - This handover is also saved as memory next-api-context-slice.

Honeycomb MCP Server - Observability Data Query Interface

<role>
You are an observability assistant for Honeycomb users. You investigate production behavior — performance, errors, deployment impact, alert state — by querying real telemetry through these tools. The workspace's actual state is only knowable through tool calls; do not reason from priors about what services, datasets, or alerts exist.

When the user names a dataset, span, or service, treat it as a starting point for discovery, not a license to skip it. The right span name within a dataset is rarely obvious from the dataset name alone, and aggregating the wrong attribute or the wrong span is the most common cause of misleading answers.
</role>

Span tools work across all trace-aware datasets in scope without needing to know which dataset to target.

1	# Upstream Host & Auth-Context Resolution
2	
3	How the CLI decides *which host to dial* and *which login (auth context) to
4	authenticate as* for every upstream call. The goal is one mental model:
5	
6	> An **auth context** is a login to one **core** (the identity provider /
7	> login server). Every upstream call resolves to some host. That host either
8	> **is** a core — use the active context's core directly — or it is a
9	> **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts via a
10	> `/.well-known` blob, so the CLI picks the context whose core is trusted and
11	> exchanges that context's token for the resource.
12	
13	There is no separate "auth system" per service. There is one identity model
14	(`contexts.json`, keyed on `CoreURL`) and a set of resource servers that
15	accept a core's JWTs.
16	
17	## The pieces
18	
19	| Role | Service (prod / staging) | Hit by | Trusted-core discovery |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| **Core** — IdP **and** control-plane API, co-located | `entire-core` (`us.auth.entire.io`) | `org` / `repo` / `project` / `grant`, `auth *`, `login` | none needed — the host *is* the core |
22	| **Resource: git cluster** | `entire-server` / `entiredb` | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) | `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` |
23	| **Resource: web/data API** | `entire.io` (`partial.to`) | `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` | **none today** — see [Deferred](#deferred) |
24	
25	`contexts.json` (`$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/contexts.json`, shared with entiredb's
26	CLIs) stores each login as `{Name, CoreURL, Handle, KeychainService}` plus a
27	`CurrentContext` pointer. `CoreURL` is the JWT `iss` — the core that minted the
28	token. `entire auth use <ctx>` flips `CurrentContext`.
29	
30	## Resolution per call type
31	
32	### Git cluster (done — `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`)
33	
34	`ResolveContextForCluster(host)` fetches+caches the cluster's
35	`/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`, reads `core_urls`, then selects the
36	context: active-context-wins if its `CoreURL` is among the cores, else the
37	sole eligible context, else an error (zero → login hint; ambiguous → asks for
38	`auth use`). The token is then exchanged for the cluster.
39	
40	### Control plane (done — this slice)
41	
42	The host *is* a core, so there is no discovery. `coreapi.New()` consults
43	`auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()`, which mirrors `auth status`:
44	
45	1. **active context** → its `CoreURL`, with a **per-context refreshing**
46	   bearer (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`): the token manager is keyed on
47	   `c.CoreURL` as issuer, so store reads and refresh/STS hit the right core,
48	   and an expired access token is silently re-minted from the stored refresh
49	   token. This is what makes `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retarget
50	   `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant`.
51	2. **else** (no active context) → the configured auth origin
52	   (`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` or the default) + `TokenForResource` — the
53	   pre-contexts fallback.
54	
55	`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` is the fallback host, **not** an override: a token
56	minted by the active context's core can't authenticate against a different
57	host, so the active context always wins when present. (At login time the env
58	var still chooses where to authenticate, and the resulting context's `CoreURL`
59	*is* that host — so local-dev / split-host setups keep working.)
60	
61	Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` (resolver),
62	`cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go` (per-context refreshing provider),
63	`internal/coreapi/client.go` (`New()` + `providerSource`),
64	`cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go` (`AuthBaseURLOverridden`).
65	
66	Why the per-context path and not the singleton manager: the singleton
67	(`auth/exchange.go:defaultManager`) is built once with `Issuer =
68	api.AuthBaseURL()`. When the active context lives on a *different* core, both
69	its token-store reads and its STS/refresh endpoint are keyed on the wrong
70	host. The per-context provider fixes that by keying on `c.CoreURL`.
71	
72	## Deferred: the web/data API (`entire.io`)
73	
74	`activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` dial `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL`
75	(default `entire.io`) and statically resolve their token. `entire.io` is a
76	**resource server** — it validates incoming JWTs against statically-configured
77	trusted issuers (`ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` + `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS`) and a
78	fixed audience (`ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE`, e.g. `entire-web-api`) — but it
79	does **not advertise** any of this. So the CLI can't map an `entire.io` host
80	back to a core/context the way it does for a git cluster.
81	
82	To close the gap (so `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity`
83	auto-selects the right context without also setting `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`):
84	
85	1. **Server**: `entire.io` grows a `/.well-known/entire-api.json` advertising
86	   its trust roots. Unlike the cluster blob (`core_urls` only), the API blob
87	   must also carry the **audience** the CLI exchanges for:
88	   ```json
89	   {
90	     "issuer": "https://us.auth.partial.to",
91	     "trusted_issuers": ["https://us.auth.partial.to", "https://eu.auth.partial.to"],
92	     "audience": "entire-web-api",
93	     "jwks_uri": "https://us.auth.partial.to/.well-known/jwks.json"
94	   }
95	   ```
96	2. **CLI**: generalize the cluster resolver into a shared "host → trusted
97	   issuers → pick context" path whose *source* of trusted issuers is pluggable
98	   (cluster.json / api.json / the core itself), then exchange the context's
99	   token for the advertised audience via `auth.TokenForResource`. Wire it into
100	   the `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` constructors
101	   (`NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `dispatch.NewCloudClient`, `search.Search`).
102	
103	`ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` names the resource host to dial (the discovery target);
104	the context is then chosen from the issuers that host advertises. It does not
105	need to be paired with `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` once discovery exists — that is
106	the whole point of the well-known.
107

# Upstream Host & Auth-Context Resolution

How the CLI decides *which host to dial* and *which login (auth context) to
authenticate as* for every upstream call. The goal is one mental model:

> An **auth context** is a login to one **core** (the identity provider /
> login server). Every upstream call resolves to some host. That host either
> **is** a core — use the active context's core directly — or it is a
> **resource server** that advertises which cores it trusts via a
> `/.well-known` blob, so the CLI picks the context whose core is trusted and
> exchanges that context's token for the resource.

There is no separate "auth system" per service. There is one identity model
(`contexts.json`, keyed on `CoreURL`) and a set of resource servers that
accept a core's JWTs.

## The pieces

| Role | Service (prod / staging) | Hit by | Trusted-core discovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** — IdP **and** control-plane API, co-located | `entire-core` (`us.auth.entire.io`) | `org` / `repo` / `project` / `grant`, `auth *`, `login` | none needed — the host *is* the core |
| **Resource: git cluster** | `entire-server` / `entiredb` | `git-remote-entire` (clone/push) | `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json` → `core_urls` |
| **Resource: web/data API** | `entire.io` (`partial.to`) | `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` | **none today** — see [Deferred](#deferred) |

`contexts.json` (`$ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR/contexts.json`, shared with entiredb's
CLIs) stores each login as `{Name, CoreURL, Handle, KeychainService}` plus a
`CurrentContext` pointer. `CoreURL` is the JWT `iss` — the core that minted the
token. `entire auth use <ctx>` flips `CurrentContext`.

## Resolution per call type

### Git cluster (done — `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`)

`ResolveContextForCluster(host)` fetches+caches the cluster's
`/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`, reads `core_urls`, then selects the
context: active-context-wins if its `CoreURL` is among the cores, else the
sole eligible context, else an error (zero → login hint; ambiguous → asks for
`auth use`). The token is then exchanged for the cluster.

### Control plane (done — this slice)

The host *is* a core, so there is no discovery. `coreapi.New()` consults
`auth.ResolveControlPlaneTarget()`, which mirrors `auth status`:

1. **active context** → its `CoreURL`, with a **per-context refreshing**
   bearer (`auth.NewRefreshingLoginProvider`): the token manager is keyed on
   `c.CoreURL` as issuer, so store reads and refresh/STS hit the right core,
   and an expired access token is silently re-minted from the stored refresh
   token. This is what makes `entire auth use <ctx>` actually retarget
   `org`/`repo`/`project`/`grant`.
2. **else** (no active context) → the configured auth origin
   (`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` or the default) + `TokenForResource` — the
   pre-contexts fallback.

`ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` is the fallback host, **not** an override: a token
minted by the active context's core can't authenticate against a different
host, so the active context always wins when present. (At login time the env
var still chooses where to authenticate, and the resulting context's `CoreURL`
*is* that host — so local-dev / split-host setups keep working.)

Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/auth/control_plane.go` (resolver),
`cmd/entire/cli/auth/refresh.go` (per-context refreshing provider),
`internal/coreapi/client.go` (`New()` + `providerSource`),
`cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go` (`AuthBaseURLOverridden`).

Why the per-context path and not the singleton manager: the singleton
(`auth/exchange.go:defaultManager`) is built once with `Issuer =
api.AuthBaseURL()`. When the active context lives on a *different* core, both
its token-store reads and its STS/refresh endpoint are keyed on the wrong
host. The per-context provider fixes that by keying on `c.CoreURL`.

## Deferred: the web/data API (`entire.io`)

`activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` dial `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL`
(default `entire.io`) and statically resolve their token. `entire.io` is a
**resource server** — it validates incoming JWTs against statically-configured
trusted issuers (`ENTIRE_CORE_BASE_URL` + `ENTIRE_CORE_TRUSTED_ISSUERS`) and a
fixed audience (`ENTIRE_CORE_JWT_AUDIENCE`, e.g. `entire-web-api`) — but it
does **not advertise** any of this. So the CLI can't map an `entire.io` host
back to a core/context the way it does for a git cluster.

To close the gap (so `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to entire activity`
auto-selects the right context without also setting `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL`):

1. **Server**: `entire.io` grows a `/.well-known/entire-api.json` advertising
   its trust roots. Unlike the cluster blob (`core_urls` only), the API blob
   must also carry the **audience** the CLI exchanges for:
   ```json
   {
     "issuer": "https://us.auth.partial.to",
     "trusted_issuers": ["https://us.auth.partial.to", "https://eu.auth.partial.to"],
     "audience": "entire-web-api",
     "jwks_uri": "https://us.auth.partial.to/.well-known/jwks.json"
   }
   ```
2. **CLI**: generalize the cluster resolver into a shared "host → trusted
   issuers → pick context" path whose *source* of trusted issuers is pluggable
   (cluster.json / api.json / the core itself), then exchange the context's
   token for the advertised audience via `auth.TokenForResource`. Wire it into
   the `activity` / `search` / `trail` / `dispatch` constructors
   (`NewAuthenticatedAPIClient`, `dispatch.NewCloudClient`, `search.Search`).

`ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` names the resource host to dial (the discovery target);
the context is then chosen from the issuers that host advertises. It does not
need to be paired with `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` once discovery exists — that is
the whole point of the well-known.

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7	
8		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/api"
9		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
10	)
11	
12	// NewAuthenticatedAPIClient creates an API client targeting api.BaseURL()
13	// (the data API origin) carrying a token valid for that audience.
14	//
15	// Resolution: looks up the core token from the keyring, then either uses
16	// it directly (single-host setup, or when the core token's `aud` already
17	// covers api.BaseURL()) or performs an RFC 8693 token exchange against
18	// the auth host to obtain a token scoped to the data API. Exchanged
19	// tokens are cached in-memory keyed off the wire-affecting fields of
20	// the request — see tokenmanager.cacheKey for the precise key shape.
21	//
22	// Pass insecureHTTP=true to allow plain HTTP base URLs for local
23	// development. Both api.BaseURL() and api.AuthBaseURL() are validated:
24	// the bearer travels to the data host on resource requests, and the
25	// core token travels to the auth host during the exchange step.
26	func NewAuthenticatedAPIClient(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool) (*api.Client, error) {
27		dataURL, authURL := api.BaseURL(), api.AuthBaseURL()
28		if insecureHTTP {
29			auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()
30		} else {
31			if err := api.RequireSecureURL(dataURL); err != nil {
32				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base URL check: %w", err)
33			}
34			if authURL != dataURL {
35				if err := api.RequireSecureURL(authURL); err != nil {
36					return nil, fmt.Errorf("auth base URL check: %w", err)
37				}
38			}
39		}
40	
41		// tokenmanager validates Resource as a strict origin URL; strip any path
42		// the operator may have included in ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL before handing
43		// it across the package boundary.
44		token, err := auth.TokenForResource(ctx, api.OriginOnly(dataURL))
45		if err != nil {
46			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
47				// Wrap the original err (not the sentinel) so any context
48				// the tokenmanager attached — keyring backend message,
49				// expired-token reason — survives to the caller. The
50				// errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) chain is preserved
51				// because err already wraps the sentinel; replacing it
52				// with the bare sentinel would drop that context for
53				// zero behavioural gain.
54				return nil, fmt.Errorf("not logged in (run 'entire login' first): %w", err)
55			}
56			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve API token: %w", err)
57		}
58	
59		return api.NewClient(token), nil
60	}

1	// Package clusterdiscovery resolves the trusted entire-core URLs that a
2	// given entire-server cluster will accept JWTs from, by hitting the
3	// cluster's /.well-known/entire-cluster.json endpoint. Used on the
4	// cold-boot path where contexts.json doesn't yet bind a cluster to a
5	// context, so we can tell the user *which* core(s) to log into instead
6	// of leaving them to guess --base-url.
7	package clusterdiscovery
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"encoding/json"
12		"errors"
13		"fmt"
14		"net/http"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	// Path mirrors server/cluster_discovery.go: the cluster advertises which
19	// entire-core URLs it accepts as JWT issuers.
20	const Path = "/.well-known/entire-cluster.json"
21	
22	// DebugFunc is the shape of the optional debug-log callback callers pass
23	// in. It mirrors fmt.Printf-style formatting so each caller can plug in
24	// its own env-var-gated logger (e.g. the [git-remote-entire] /
25	// [entiredb] prefixed debugfs gated by ENTIRE_DEBUG). Pass nil to
26	// suppress debug output.
27	type DebugFunc func(format string, args ...any)
28	
29	// Response is the parsed shape of /.well-known/entire-cluster.json. New
30	// fields may be added by the server; unknown ones are ignored.
31	type Response struct {
32		CoreURLs []string `json:"core_urls"`
33	}
34	
35	// Sentinel errors returned by Discover so callers can branch on the
36	// failure mode (and surface different operator messages) without
37	// stringly-typing the diagnosis.
38	var (
39		// ErrUnreachable wraps any transport-level failure dialing the
40		// cluster (DNS, connection refused, TLS handshake, timeout). The
41		// host might be a typo or a real-but-down cluster — the client
42		// can't tell, and operators get the same nudge for both.
43		ErrUnreachable = errors.New("cluster unreachable")
44		// ErrNoIssuers means the cluster responded HTTP 503 — up but with
45		// an empty trusted-issuers configuration. Operator misconfig,
46		// not a client problem.
47		ErrNoIssuers = errors.New("cluster does not advertise any trusted login servers")
48		// ErrNoCoreURLs means the cluster responded HTTP 200 but the JSON
49		// carried an empty (or absent) core_urls list. Distinct from
50		// ErrNoIssuers because the operator fix is different — the
51		// response shape is wrong, rather than the 503 surface being
52		// served.
53		ErrNoCoreURLs = errors.New("cluster advertises no trusted core URLs")
54	)
55	
56	// Discover fetches and parses the cluster's
57	// /.well-known/entire-cluster.json. On success returns the parsed body
58	// with a non-empty CoreURLs list. On failure returns one of the
59	// sentinel errors above (wrapped with context) or a wrapped decode
60	// error for malformed JSON. Network failures are wrapped under
61	// ErrUnreachable so the caller can render the "looks unreachable"
62	// nudge without string-matching.
63	//
64	// debugf is optional; nil suppresses debug output.
65	func Discover(ctx context.Context, clusterHost string, c *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) (*Response, error) {
66		if debugf == nil {
67			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
68		}
69		url := "https://" + clusterHost + Path
70		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
71		if err != nil {
72			return nil, fmt.Errorf("build discovery request: %w", err)
73		}
74		resp, err := c.Do(req)
75		if err != nil {
76			debugf("cluster discovery: %v", err)
77			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrUnreachable, err)
78		}
79		defer resp.Body.Close()
80	
81		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusServiceUnavailable {
82			return nil, ErrNoIssuers
83		}
84		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
85			debugf("cluster discovery: HTTP %d from %s", resp.StatusCode, url)
86			return nil, fmt.Errorf("HTTP %d from %s", resp.StatusCode, url)
87		}
88		var body Response
89		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
90			debugf("cluster discovery: decode: %v", err)
91			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode %s: %w", url, err)
92		}
93		if len(body.CoreURLs) == 0 {
94			debugf("cluster discovery: no core_urls in response from %s", url)
95			return nil, ErrNoCoreURLs
96		}
97		return &body, nil
98	}
99	
100	// RenderLoginHint formats a fatal-ready message describing which
101	// entire-core URLs an operator can log into to gain credentials for
102	// clusterHost. The output is stable (one indented URL per line) so
103	// callers can pattern-match in tests.
104	func RenderLoginHint(clusterHost string, coreURLs []string) string {
105		var b strings.Builder
106		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "no auth context for cluster %s. This cluster accepts logins from:\n", clusterHost)
107		for _, u := range coreURLs {
108			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %s\n", u)
109		}
110		fmt.Fprint(&b, "\nAuthenticate against one of those login servers and re-run your command:\n"+
111			"  ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=<url> entire login\n"+
112			"or, if you already have a login there, switch to it with `entire auth use <context>`.")
113		return b.String()
114	}

1	package clusterdiscovery
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"net/http"
8		"sort"
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/contexts"
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/entireclient/discovery"
13	)
14	
15	// ResolveContextForCluster picks the local login context to authenticate
16	// git operations against clusterHost.
17	//
18	// It separates two concerns that used to be conflated in a single
19	// cluster→context binding:
20	//
21	//   - Which control plane(s) front the cluster — an objective infra fact.
22	//     Discovered from the cluster's /.well-known/entire-cluster.json and
23	//     cached in cluster_cores.json (see discovery.ClusterCoresCache) with
24	//     a long TTL, since a cluster's home core is near-static. On a cache
25	//     miss or expiry we re-fetch; if the re-fetch fails we fall back to
26	//     the stale cached cores rather than break the op.
27	//
28	//   - Which of the user's accounts to use — recomputed every call from the
29	//     live contexts, never persisted. So a user with several accounts is
30	//     never silently pinned to one identity.
31	//
32	// Account selection (selectContext):
33	//
34	//  1. If the active context (current_context) is issued by one of the
35	//     cluster's cores, use it. This is the explicit lever: `entire auth
36	//     use <name>` chooses the identity for every cluster that context's
37	//     core fronts.
38	//  2. Otherwise gather every local context eligible for the cluster (its
39	//     CoreURL is among the advertised cores):
40	//     - exactly one  → use it (the common single-account case);
41	//     - none         → error with the login hint listing the cluster's cores;
42	//     - more than one → error asking the user to pick with `entire auth use`,
43	//     rather than silently guessing an account.
44	//
45	// We never fall back to an active context whose core does NOT front the
46	// cluster: the cluster would reject the exchanged token as "unknown
47	// cluster_host", and silently authenticating a staging identity against a
48	// prod cluster (or vice versa) is exactly the confusion the /.well-known
49	// lookup exists to prevent.
50	//
51	// debugf is optional; nil suppresses debug output.
52	func ResolveContextForCluster(ctx context.Context, configDir, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) (*contexts.Context, error) {
53		if debugf == nil {
54			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
55		}
56		f, err := contexts.Load(configDir)
57		if err != nil {
58			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load contexts: %w", err)
59		}
60	
61		coreURLs, err := resolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
62		if err != nil {
63			return nil, err
64		}
65	
66		return selectContext(f, clusterHost, coreURLs, debugf)
67	}
68	
69	// ResolveClusterCores returns the trusted control-plane core URLs that
70	// front clusterHost, using the same cache-then-/.well-known discovery as
71	// ResolveContextForCluster (see resolveClusterCores). Exported for callers
72	// that need the cluster's trusted-core set without account selection — e.g.
73	// the ENTIRE_TOKEN path validates that the env token's audience is one of
74	// these before exchanging it, so an unverified JWT can't redirect the
75	// token exchange to an attacker-chosen host.
76	func ResolveClusterCores(ctx context.Context, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) ([]string, error) {
77		if debugf == nil {
78			debugf = func(string, ...any) {}
79		}
80		return resolveClusterCores(ctx, cacheDir, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
81	}
82	
83	// resolveClusterCores returns the control-plane core URLs that front
84	// clusterHost, from cluster_cores.json when fresh, otherwise via a live
85	// /.well-known fetch (which is then cached). A stale-but-present cache
86	// entry is used as a fallback when the live fetch fails, so a brief
87	// cluster outage doesn't break an operation whose cores we already knew.
88	func resolveClusterCores(ctx context.Context, cacheDir, clusterHost string, httpClient *http.Client, debugf DebugFunc) ([]string, error) {
89		cache, err := discovery.LoadClusterCores(cacheDir)
90		if err != nil {
91			// A cache read problem must not block resolution — discover live.
92			debugf("cluster-cores cache load failed: %v; discovering live", err)
93			cache = nil
94		}
95	
96		var stale []string
97		if cache != nil {
98			if urls, fresh, ok := cache.Get(clusterHost); ok {
99				if fresh {
100					debugf("cluster %s cores from cache: %v", clusterHost, urls)
101					return urls, nil
102				}
103				stale = urls
104				debugf("cluster %s cores cache expired; re-fetching /.well-known", clusterHost)
105			}
106		}
107	
108		body, err := Discover(ctx, clusterHost, httpClient, debugf)
109		if err != nil {
110			if stale != nil {
111				debugf("discovery for %s failed (%v); falling back to stale cached cores %v", clusterHost, err, stale)
112				return stale, nil
113			}
114			return nil, formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost, err)
115		}
116	
117		if mErr := discovery.ModifyClusterCores(cacheDir, func(c discovery.ClusterCoresCache) error {
118			c.Set(clusterHost, body.CoreURLs)
119			return nil
120		}); mErr != nil {
121			// Non-fatal: we resolved the cores, the next call just re-fetches.
122			debugf("cluster-cores cache write for %s failed: %v", clusterHost, mErr)
123		}
124		return body.CoreURLs, nil
125	}
126	
127	// selectContext applies the account-selection rules over the cluster's
128	// advertised cores. See ResolveContextForCluster for the rationale.
129	func selectContext(f *contexts.File, clusterHost string, coreURLs []string, debugf DebugFunc) (*contexts.Context, error) {
130		eligible := eligibleContexts(f, coreURLs)
131	
132		// 1. Active context wins when it's eligible for this cluster.
133		if current := f.Find(f.CurrentContext); current != nil {
134			for _, c := range eligible {
135				if c.Name == current.Name {
136					debugf("cluster %s -> active context %s", clusterHost, current.Name)
137					return current, nil
138				}
139			}
140		}
141	
142		// 2. Otherwise the eligible set decides.
143		switch len(eligible) {
144		case 0:
145			return nil, errors.New(RenderLoginHint(clusterHost, coreURLs))
146		case 1:
147			debugf("cluster %s -> sole eligible context %s", clusterHost, eligible[0].Name)
148			return eligible[0], nil
149		default:
150			return nil, ambiguousContextError(clusterHost, eligible)
151		}
152	}
153	
154	// eligibleContexts returns the local contexts whose core is among coreURLs,
155	// de-duplicated by name. Order is unspecified — callers either use the sole
156	// element or report the whole set, never index [0] as a silent winner.
157	func eligibleContexts(f *contexts.File, coreURLs []string) []*contexts.Context {
158		seen := make(map[string]bool)
159		var out []*contexts.Context
160		for _, coreURL := range coreURLs {
161			for _, c := range f.ContextsForIssuer(coreURL) {
162				if !seen[c.Name] {
163					seen[c.Name] = true
164					out = append(out, c)
165				}
166			}
167		}
168		return out
169	}
170	
171	// ambiguousContextError is returned when more than one local context could
172	// authenticate against the cluster and none is active. We refuse to guess —
173	// the user picks explicitly. Names are sorted so the message is stable.
174	func ambiguousContextError(clusterHost string, eligible []*contexts.Context) error {
175		names := make([]string, len(eligible))
176		for i, c := range eligible {
177			names[i] = c.Name
178		}
179		sort.Strings(names)
180		return fmt.Errorf("multiple login contexts can authenticate against cluster %s (%s); choose one with `entire auth use <context>` and re-run",
181			clusterHost, strings.Join(names, ", "))
182	}
183	
184	// formatDiscoveryError turns a Discover error into the message
185	// operators have always seen at this layer. Kept here (not on the
186	// sentinels themselves) so the package's errors stay machine-readable
187	// while the caller-facing strings remain centralised.
188	func formatDiscoveryError(clusterHost string, err error) error {
189		switch {
190		case errors.Is(err, ErrUnreachable):
191			return fmt.Errorf("%s doesn't look like a cluster, or it is unreachable: %w", clusterHost, err)
192		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoIssuers):
193			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s does not advertise any trusted login servers (HTTP 503 from %s); contact the cluster administrator",
194				clusterHost, Path)
195		case errors.Is(err, ErrNoCoreURLs):
196			return fmt.Errorf("cluster %s advertises no trusted core URLs (empty list at %s); contact the cluster administrator",
197				clusterHost, Path)
198		default:
199			return fmt.Errorf("cluster discovery for %s: %w", clusterHost, err)
200		}
201	}

14	// TokenRequest is the entire-CLI alias of tokenmanager.TokenRequest so
15	// callers don't have to import the underlying package for the common
16	// case. The two types are interchangeable.
17	type TokenRequest = tokenmanager.TokenRequest
18	
19	// ErrNotLoggedIn re-exports tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn so callers in
20	// the cli package can errors.Is against it without an extra import.
21	var ErrNotLoggedIn = tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn
22	
23	var (
24		managerOnce sync.Once
25		manager     *tokenmanager.Manager
26		errManager  error
27	
28		// managerForTest, when non-nil, is returned by defaultManager()
29		// instead of constructing the production manager. Guarded by
30		// managerTestMu so concurrent tests calling Set/defaultManager
31		// don't race. Production code never reads this var.
32		managerForTest *tokenmanager.Manager
33		managerTestMu  sync.Mutex
34	
35		// insecureHTTPOverride records the --insecure-http-auth opt-in.
36		// Read once when the package-level manager is built (sync.Once);
37		// callers must invoke EnableInsecureHTTP before any TokenForResource
38		// call in the same process or the override has no effect. Loopback
39		// hosts are always permitted regardless of this flag.
40		insecureHTTPOverride atomic.Bool
41	)
42	
43	// EnableInsecureHTTP relaxes the package-level manager's HTTPS guard so
44	// non-loopback http:// resources (and the auth host's STS endpoint) are
45	// permitted during token resolution. The CLI calls this when the user
46	// passes --insecure-http-auth to a command that hits the data API on a
47	// private network (e.g. a split-host local-dev box where both hosts are
48	// plain HTTP).
49	//
50	// Call before any TokenForResource invocation — the manager is built
51	// lazily on first use and the AllowInsecureHTTP setting is frozen at
52	// that point.
53	func EnableInsecureHTTP() {
54		insecureHTTPOverride.Store(true)
55	}
56	
57	// insecureHTTPEnabled reports whether EnableInsecureHTTP was called. The
58	// per-context control-plane provider (which bypasses the singleton manager)
59	// reads this so --insecure-http-auth still relaxes the HTTPS guard for a
60	// non-loopback http:// core, mirroring the singleton's AllowInsecureHTTP.
61	func insecureHTTPEnabled() bool {
62		return insecureHTTPOverride.Load()
63	}
64	
65	// SetManagerForTest installs mgr as the manager returned by
66	// defaultManager() and returns a cleanup function. Test-only.
67	func SetManagerForTest(t interface{ Helper() }, mgr *tokenmanager.Manager) func() {
68		t.Helper()
69		managerTestMu.Lock()
70		prev := managerForTest
71		managerForTest = mgr
72		managerTestMu.Unlock()
73		return func() {
74			managerTestMu.Lock()
75			managerForTest = prev
76			managerTestMu.Unlock()
77		}
78	}
79	
80	// defaultManager returns the package-level Manager built from this
81	// CLI's identity (current provider, AuthBaseURL, NewStore service
82	// name). Constructed lazily on first use so any env-var setup
83	// (ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL, ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION) lands before
84	// construction. sync.Once means later env-var changes within the same
85	// process are ignored; tests bypass the singleton via SetManagerForTest.
86	func defaultManager() (*tokenmanager.Manager, error) {
87		managerTestMu.Lock()
88		override := managerForTest
89		managerTestMu.Unlock()
90		if override != nil {
91			return override, nil
92		}
93		managerOnce.Do(func() {
94			provider := CurrentProvider()
95			issuer := api.AuthBaseURL()
96			m, err := tokenmanager.New(tokenmanager.Config{
97				Issuer:   issuer,
98				ClientID: provider.ClientID,
99				STSPath:  provider.STSPath,
100				// Context-preferring store: the manager reads the active
101				// contexts.json login (falling back to the legacy entry) so a
102				// single login authenticates every control-plane command.
103				Store:     NewContextStore(),
104				UserAgent: provider.ClientID,
105				Scope:     "cli",
106				// Auto-permit loopback http:// for local development. The
107				// EnableInsecureHTTP setter adds non-loopback http on top
108				// so split-host private-network dev (e.g. http://devbox.internal)
109				// works under --insecure-http-auth. Anything else must be
110				// https:// — STS ships the user's core token in the request
111				// body and would leak in clear otherwise.
112				AllowInsecureHTTP: isLoopbackHTTP(issuer) || insecureHTTPOverride.Load(),
113			})
114			manager = m
115			if err != nil {
116				errManager = fmt.Errorf("build token manager: %w", err)
117			}
118		})
119		return manager, errManager
120	}
121	
122	// TokenForResource returns a bearer token suitable for use against
123	// resourceBaseURL, performing an RFC 8693 token exchange when the
124	// stored core token's audience doesn't already cover that resource.
125	// See tokenmanager.Manager.Token for the full resolution rules.
126	func TokenForResource(ctx context.Context, resourceBaseURL string) (string, error) {
127		m, err := defaultManager()
128		if err != nil {
129			return "", err
130		}
131		return m.TokenForResource(ctx, resourceBaseURL) //nolint:wrapcheck // shim returns the lib error verbatim
132	}
133	
134	// isLoopbackHTTP reports whether u is an http:// URL pointing at a
135	// loopback hostname (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1). Used to scope the
136	// "auto-permit insecure HTTP" path on the tokenmanager so production
137	// misconfigurations fail loudly while loopback-only local-dev flows
138	// keep working.
139	func isLoopbackHTTP(rawURL string) bool {
140		u, err := url.Parse(rawURL)
141		if err != nil || u.Scheme != "http" {
142			return false
143		}
144		host := u.Hostname()
145		return host == "localhost" || host == "127.0.0.1" || host == "::1"
146	}

1	// Package tokenmanager orchestrates core-token storage and RFC 8693
2	// token exchanges for an OAuth 2.0 device-flow client.
3	//
4	// One Manager per CLI process. Construct it once from the embedding
5	// CLI's identity (Issuer, ClientID, STSPath, Store) and call
6	// TokenForResource / Token from data-API call sites.
7	//
8	// The package is provider-agnostic: every endpoint, identifier, and
9	// default value comes from Config. It has no env-var reads, no
10	// implicit URLs, and no embedded provider tables. Tests inject
11	// behaviour via SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest / SetRefreshForTest /
12	// SetProcessLockForTest (see testseams.go) rather than via the public
13	// Config — keeping the STS call out of the caller-controllable surface.
14	package tokenmanager
15	
16	import (
17		"context"
18		"crypto/sha256"
19		"encoding/hex"
20		"errors"
21		"fmt"
22		"net/http"
23		"net/url"
24		"os"
25		"path/filepath"
26		"strings"
27		"sync"
28		"sync/atomic"
29		"time"
30	
31		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/internal/oauthhttp"
32		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/internal/proclock"
33		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/refresh"
34		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/sts"
35		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokens"
36		"github.com/entireio/auth-go/tokenstore"
37	)
38	
39	// DefaultRequestedTokenType is the RFC 8693 §3 URI used when neither
40	// Config.RequestedTokenType nor TokenRequest.RequestedTokenType is set.
41	// :access_token is the canonical "give me an OAuth access token" URI;
42	// the wire format is the server's choice.
43	//
44	//nolint:gosec // RFC 8693 token-type URI, not a credential
45	const DefaultRequestedTokenType = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"
46	
47	// exchangeSkew is the safety margin applied when deciding whether a
48	// cached exchanged token is still usable. Set conservatively because
49	// the worst case (re-exchange one extra time per command) is cheap.
50	const exchangeSkew = 30 * time.Second
51	
52	// ErrNotLoggedIn is returned by Token / TokenForResource when no core token
53	// is present in the store, or when a stored token is expired and carries no
54	// refresh token (the session cannot be silently renewed). Callers can match
55	// on it to render a "run <login>" message.
56	var ErrNotLoggedIn = errors.New("not logged in")
57	
58	// ErrNoSTSPath is returned when an exchange is needed but Config.STSPath
59	// is empty. Single-host deployments hit the same-host shortcut and never
60	// reach this; split-host deployments must configure STSPath.
61	var ErrNoSTSPath = errors.New("token exchange required but Config.STSPath is empty")
62	
63	// ErrReauthRequired is returned by Token / Refresh when the stored refresh
64	// token is genuinely revoked or expired (server returned invalid_grant and
65	// a store re-read confirmed the refresh token was not concurrently
66	// rotated). Distinct from ErrNotLoggedIn — there was a credential, the
67	// session simply needs a fresh interactive login. Callers can match on it
68	// to render "your session expired, log in again".
69	var ErrReauthRequired = errors.New("reauthentication required")
70	
71	// ErrNoRefreshPath is returned when a refresh is needed but
72	// Config.RefreshPath is empty. Mirrors ErrNoSTSPath.
73	var ErrNoRefreshPath = errors.New("refresh required but Config.RefreshPath is empty")
74	
75	// Config configures a Manager.
76	type Config struct {
77		// Issuer is the auth host base URL where the device-flow login
78		// happened and STS exchanges are POSTed. Required. Doubles as the
79		// Store profile key, so a user can be logged into multiple issuers
80		// (e.g. regions / staging) without conflict.
81		Issuer string
82	
83		// ClientID identifies the public client per RFC 6749 §2.3.1 / §3.2.1.
84		// Sent on STS exchanges via the client_id form field. Required.
85		ClientID string
86	
87		// STSPath is the path on Issuer where token-exchange requests are
88		// POSTed. Optional: single-host deployments never trigger an
89		// exchange (the same-host shortcut wins) so they can leave it
90		// empty. When empty and an exchange is attempted, runExchange
91		// returns ErrNoSTSPath rather than POSTing to a bogus URL.
92		STSPath string
93	
94		// RefreshPath is the token-endpoint path where grant_type=refresh_token
95		// is POSTed to re-mint the login JWT. Optional: when empty and a
96		// refresh is needed, runRefresh returns ErrNoRefreshPath. Often equal
97		// to STSPath or the device-flow token path, since servers typically
98		// multiplex grants at one /oauth/token.
99		RefreshPath string
100	
101		// LockDir is the directory holding the cross-process advisory lock
102		// file. Empty → os.UserCacheDir()/auth-go (falling back to the system
103		// temp dir if the user cache dir is unavailable). The lock file holds
104		// no credentials.
105		LockDir string
106	
107		// Store persists the core token. Required. Use any tokenstore.Store
108		// implementation; a per-CLI service name keeps credentials isolated
109		// from other CLIs sharing this library.
110		Store tokenstore.Store
111	
112		// RequestedTokenType is the default RFC 8693 requested_token_type
113		// URI. Empty → DefaultRequestedTokenType.
114		RequestedTokenType string
115	
116		// SubjectTokenType is the RFC 8693 subject_token_type sent on
117		// exchanges. Empty → sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken.
118		//
119		// :access_token is the RFC 8693 §3 URI for "OAuth 2.0 access token
120		// issued by the given authorization server" — exactly what the
121		// device-code grant returns into Store. The distinction from :jwt
122		// matters at the server: zitadel-oidc's STS validator (pkg/op/
123		// token_exchange.go's GetTokenIDAndSubjectFromToken) only switches on
124		// :access_token / :refresh_token / :id_token; :jwt passes the
125		// IsSupported() check upstream but silently falls through to the
126		// not-handled branch and surfaces as the (uninformative)
127		// "subject_token is invalid" error_description. Other servers
128		// generally treat :jwt and :access_token interchangeably for OAuth
129		// access tokens, so :access_token is the safer default. A caller who
130		// genuinely needs :jwt semantics (RFC 7519 JWT-as-credential rather
131		// than OAuth-issued bearer) can set this field explicitly, or bypass
132		// tokenmanager and call sts.Client.Exchange directly.
133		SubjectTokenType string
134	
135		// Scope is the default scope sent on exchanges. Empty → omitted.
136		Scope string
137	
138		// UserAgent for HTTP requests. Empty → none.
139		UserAgent string
140	
141		// AllowInsecureHTTP permits exchanges against http:// issuers. Off
142		// by default — STS calls ship the user's core token in the request
143		// body and must be TLS-protected. Only flip this for local/dev
144		// deployments pinned to loopback.
145		AllowInsecureHTTP bool
146	
147		// Transport overrides the http.RoundTripper used for STS calls.
148		// Useful for installing a debug logger or proxy. nil →
149		// http.DefaultTransport. Replaces the previous HTTPClient field —
150		// see sts.Client.Transport for the security rationale.
151		Transport http.RoundTripper
152	}
153	
154	func (c Config) validate() error {
155		switch {
156		case strings.TrimSpace(c.Issuer) == "":
157			return errors.New("Config.Issuer is required")
158		case strings.TrimSpace(c.ClientID) == "":
159			return errors.New("Config.ClientID is required")
160		case c.Store == nil:
161			return errors.New("Config.Store is required")
162		}
163		return nil
164	}
165	
166	// exchangeFunc / nowFuncType are named so we can hold them in
167	// atomic.Pointer values. Storing the override behind an
168	// atomic.Pointer rather than a plain field plus mu lets the hot read
169	// paths (runExchange, m.now) avoid taking the lock — they were
170	// previously racing with SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest.
171	type exchangeFunc func(ctx context.Context, req sts.ExchangeRequest) (*tokens.TokenSet, error)
172	type nowFuncType func() time.Time
173	
174	// ProcessLock serialises credential mutations (refresh, save, delete)
175	// across processes. Acquire blocks until the lock is held or ctx is done,
176	// returning an idempotent release func. On error the returned release func
177	// is nil and must not be called. The default implementation is a file lock
178	// (internal/proclock); SetProcessLockForTest swaps a fake.
179	type ProcessLock interface {
180		Acquire(ctx context.Context) (release func(), err error)
181	}
182	
183	type refreshFunc func(ctx context.Context, req refresh.Request) (*tokens.TokenSet, error)
184	
185	// Manager orchestrates core-token storage and STS exchanges. Safe for
186	// concurrent use.
187	type Manager struct {
188		cfg Config
189	
190		mu    sync.Mutex
191		cache map[cacheKey]cachedToken
192	
193		// Test seams. Set only via SetExchangeForTest / SetNowForTest,
194		// both of which require a testing.TB to discourage production
195		// callers from synthesising a fake TB to bypass STS. Held behind
196		// atomic.Pointer so hot-path reads (runExchange, now) don't race
197		// against test setup/teardown.
198		exchangeOverride atomic.Pointer[exchangeFunc]
199		nowOverride      atomic.Pointer[nowFuncType]
200	
201		// refreshMu is the in-process single-flight gate for re-mints. Held
202		// across the cross-process lock + grant so concurrent goroutines
203		// coalesce onto one re-mint (the second waiter re-reads a fresh token).
204		refreshMu sync.Mutex
205	
206		// Refresh + process-lock test seams; see SetRefreshForTest /
207		// SetProcessLockForTest. Same atomic.Pointer rationale as above.
208		refreshOverride atomic.Pointer[refreshFunc]
209		lockOverride    atomic.Pointer[ProcessLock]
210	
211		lockOnce    sync.Once
212		defaultLock ProcessLock
213	}
214	
215	// now returns the manager's effective clock. Tests can replace it via
216	// SetNowForTest; production callers always get time.Now.
217	func (m *Manager) now() time.Time {
218		if p := m.nowOverride.Load(); p != nil {
219			return (*p)()
220		}
221		return time.Now()
222	}

224	// New builds a Manager from cfg. Returns an error when required
225	// fields are missing or Issuer is not an absolute URL.
226	//
227	// Issuer is normalized via RFC 3986 §6.2.2 (lowercase scheme/host,
228	// default-port stripped, no trailing slash) before being used as the
229	// Store profile key and as the same-host shortcut comparison. Without
230	// this, two Managers configured with cosmetically-different issuers
231	// (`https://auth.example.com/` vs `https://auth.example.com`) would
232	// write to different keyring entries but compare equal for the
233	// shortcut — one Manager handing out the other's tokens.
234	func New(cfg Config) (*Manager, error) {
235		if err := cfg.validate(); err != nil {
236			return nil, err
237		}
238		// Hold Issuer to the same origin-URL contract as TokenRequest.Resource:
239		// userinfo, path, query, fragment all forbidden. The same-host shortcut
240		// (Token) byte-compares the normalised Resource against cfg.Issuer; an
241		// Issuer that still carries userinfo or a path silently fails that
242		// equality even when the caller's Resource is the "same" origin.
243		normIssuer, err := oauthhttp.ValidateOriginURL(cfg.Issuer, cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP, "Config.Issuer")
244		if err != nil {
245			return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // pass through with field-named message
246		}
247		cfg.Issuer = normIssuer
248		if cfg.RequestedTokenType == "" {
249			cfg.RequestedTokenType = DefaultRequestedTokenType
250		}
251		if cfg.SubjectTokenType == "" {
252			cfg.SubjectTokenType = sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken
253		}
254		return &Manager{cfg: cfg, cache: map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}}, nil
255	}
256	
257	// Issuer returns the configured issuer URL.
258	func (m *Manager) Issuer() string { return m.cfg.Issuer }
259	
260	// SaveCoreToken persists the full device-flow token bundle under the
261	// configured Issuer. Takes the entire tokens.TokenSet (rather than
262	// just the access token) so RefreshToken, absolute ExpiresAt, and
263	// Scope survive the round-trip through the keyring — earlier versions
264	// dropped these fields silently, blocking refresh-token support and
265	// losing the wire-side expiry hint for opaque tokens.
266	//
267	// AccessToken is required (rejected here rather than letting it
268	// surface as a confusing "Bearer <empty>" later). The tokens.TokenSet
269	// is otherwise stored verbatim; consumers can read the persisted
270	// fields back via Store.LoadTokens.
271	//
272	// On successful save the in-memory exchange cache is cleared so a
273	// re-login under a different identity can't return the previous user's
274	// exchanged tokens. The cacheKey already binds entries to the core
275	// token's SHA-256 hash, so this is defence-in-depth — see
276	// TestSaveCoreToken_ClearsExchangeCache.
277	//
278	// SaveCoreToken is serialised against in-flight refreshes by acquiring
279	// refreshMu and the cross-process lock before mutating the store. Without
280	// this, a refresh whose grant is mid-flight could land its persist after
281	// a concurrent SaveCoreToken (re-login) and overwrite the new identity
282	// with the old account's refreshed credentials. Lock ordering matches
283	// refreshLocked: refreshMu first, then processLock. Can block up to
284	// ~30s under contention and may return a wrapped lock error. The
285	// empty-AccessToken check fires before lock acquisition so an obviously
286	// bad call doesn't touch the filesystem.
287	func (m *Manager) SaveCoreToken(t tokens.TokenSet) error {
288		if t.AccessToken == "" {
289			return errors.New("save core token: AccessToken is empty")
290		}
291		m.refreshMu.Lock()
292		defer m.refreshMu.Unlock()
293		release, err := m.processLock().Acquire(context.Background())
294		if err != nil {
295			return fmt.Errorf("save core token: acquire lock: %w", err)
296		}
297		defer release()
298		return m.saveCoreTokenLocked(t)
299	}
300	
301	// saveCoreTokenLocked is the lock-free persist path. Caller MUST hold
302	// refreshMu and the process lock. Used by SaveCoreToken (which acquires
303	// them) and by persistRefreshed (which runs inside refreshLocked where
304	// both are already held — a recursive lock attempt here would
305	// self-deadlock).
306	//
307	// The empty-AccessToken check is duplicated here as defence in depth
308	// because the locked variant is also reachable from persistRefreshed.
309	func (m *Manager) saveCoreTokenLocked(t tokens.TokenSet) error {
310		if t.AccessToken == "" {
311			return errors.New("save core token: AccessToken is empty")
312		}
313		if err := m.cfg.Store.SaveTokens(m.cfg.Issuer, t); err != nil {
314			return fmt.Errorf("save core token: %w", err)
315		}
316		m.mu.Lock()
317		m.cache = map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}
318		m.mu.Unlock()
319		return nil
320	}
321	
322	// LookupCoreToken returns the stored core token, or "" if none is
323	// stored. A nil-return-no-error mirrors how callers expect
324	// "not-logged-in" to look.
325	func (m *Manager) LookupCoreToken() (string, error) {
326		t, err := m.cfg.Store.LoadTokens(m.cfg.Issuer)
327		if errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) {
328			return "", nil
329		}
330		if err != nil {
331			return "", fmt.Errorf("load core token: %w", err)
332		}
333		return t.AccessToken, nil
334	}

336	// Refresh ensures a fresh login JWT, re-minting it from the stored refresh
337	// token when the current one is expired or near expiry, and returns it.
338	// It is idempotent when the token is already fresh (a cheap store read, no
339	// grant). Returns ErrNotLoggedIn when no credential is stored (or an
340	// expired one carries no refresh token), and ErrReauthRequired when the
341	// refresh token is revoked/expired.
342	//
343	// Callers can use this to warm the session at startup and surface a
344	// re-login prompt before the first data call rather than mid-request.
345	//
346	// Expiry is judged from the login JWT's exp claim. Opaque (non-JWT)
347	// stored tokens have no client-visible expiry, so they are treated as
348	// live and never trigger a re-mint — the refresh tier assumes a JWT login
349	// token (as in the three-tier session model).
350	func (m *Manager) Refresh(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
351		return m.ensureFreshLogin(ctx)
352	}

354	// DeleteCoreToken removes the stored core token and any cached exchanges
355	// derived from it.
356	//
357	// Order matters within the locked region: the keyring delete runs first,
358	// then the in-memory cache is cleared. If the keyring delete fails the
359	// cache is left alone — clearing it pre-emptively would create a window
360	// where the CLI thinks it's logged out (no cache entries) but the keyring
361	// still hands out the core token to the next process.
362	//
363	// DeleteCoreToken is serialised against in-flight refreshes by acquiring
364	// refreshMu and the cross-process lock before mutating the store. Without
365	// this, a refresh whose grant is mid-flight could land its persist after
366	// a concurrent logout and resurrect the deleted session. Lock ordering
367	// matches refreshLocked: refreshMu first, then processLock. Can block up
368	// to ~30s under contention and may return a wrapped lock error.
369	func (m *Manager) DeleteCoreToken() error {
370		m.refreshMu.Lock()
371		defer m.refreshMu.Unlock()
372		release, err := m.processLock().Acquire(context.Background())
373		if err != nil {
374			return fmt.Errorf("delete core token: acquire lock: %w", err)
375		}
376		defer release()
377		return m.deleteCoreTokenLocked()
378	}
379	
380	// deleteCoreTokenLocked is the lock-free delete path. Caller MUST hold
381	// refreshMu and the process lock.
382	func (m *Manager) deleteCoreTokenLocked() error {
383		if err := m.cfg.Store.DeleteTokens(m.cfg.Issuer); err != nil {
384			return fmt.Errorf("delete core token: %w", err)
385		}
386		m.mu.Lock()
387		m.cache = map[cacheKey]cachedToken{}
388		m.mu.Unlock()
389		return nil
390	}

392	// TokenRequest customises one Token call. Empty fields fall back to
393	// Config defaults.
394	type TokenRequest struct {
395		// Resource is the origin where the bearer will be presented.
396		// Required. Used for the same-host shortcut, the JWT-aud shortcut,
397		// and as part of the cache key.
398		Resource string
399	
400		// Audience is the wire-level RFC 8693 audience parameter. Empty →
401		// omitted (the AS picks). Independent of Resource — most callers
402		// leave Audience empty.
403		Audience string
404	
405		// RequestedTokenType overrides Config.RequestedTokenType for this
406		// call. Empty → Config default.
407		RequestedTokenType string
408	
409		// Scope overrides Config.Scope for this call. Empty → Config default.
410		Scope string
411	}

413	// TokenForResource is a convenience for Token using only Resource.
414	func (m *Manager) TokenForResource(ctx context.Context, resourceBaseURL string) (string, error) {
415		return m.Token(ctx, TokenRequest{Resource: resourceBaseURL})
416	}
417	
418	// Token resolves a bearer token for use against req.Resource,
419	// performing an RFC 8693 exchange when needed.
420	//
421	// Resolution rules:
422	//
423	//  1. No core token in the store → ErrNotLoggedIn.
424	//  2. Core (login JWT) expired or near expiry → transparently re-mint it
425	//     from the stored refresh token (see Refresh). No refresh token →
426	//     ErrNotLoggedIn; refresh token revoked/expired → ErrReauthRequired;
427	//     Config.RefreshPath unset → ErrNoRefreshPath.
428	//  3. m.Issuer() == req.Resource (and req.Audience is empty) → use
429	//     the core token directly. Single-host deployments hit this path.
430	//  4. Core token's `aud` claim already includes req.Resource → use
431	//     the core token directly. Multi-audience tokens skip exchange.
432	//  5. Otherwise → RFC 8693 token exchange.
433	//
434	// Successful exchanges are cached in-memory keyed by (core token,
435	// resource, audience, requested-token-type, scope) until expiry.
436	func (m *Manager) Token(ctx context.Context, req TokenRequest) (string, error) {
437		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Resource) == "" {
438			return "", errors.New("TokenRequest.Resource is required")
439		}
440		normResource, err := oauthhttp.ValidateOriginURL(req.Resource, m.cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP, "TokenRequest.Resource")
441		if err != nil {
442			return "", err
443		}
444	
445		core, err := m.ensureFreshLogin(ctx)
446		if err != nil {
447			return "", err
448		}
449	
450		// m.cfg.Issuer was normalized at New() time, so no re-normalize here.
451		if req.Audience == "" && m.cfg.Issuer == normResource {
452			return core, nil
453		}
454		if req.Audience == "" && coreTokenAudienceIncludes(core, normResource) {
455			return core, nil
456		}
457	
458		resolved := m.resolve(req)
459		resolved.Resource = normResource
460		// Default Audience to the normalized resource URI. RFC 8693 §2.1
461		// treats audience and resource as overlapping ways to identify the
462		// target service, but some AS implementations (notably zitadel-OIDC-
463		// backed servers — entire-core as of 2026-05) require audience to
464		// be populated and reject the request with
465		// "invalid_target: audience is required" when only resource is
466		// present. Applying the default here, AFTER the same-host and
467		// JWT-aud shortcuts above, means single-host deployments still
468		// return the core token unchanged without setting audience — only
469		// requests that actually go to the STS endpoint get the populated
470		// audience. Callers that explicitly set Audience to something
471		// different are preserved verbatim.
472		if resolved.Audience == "" {
473			resolved.Audience = normResource
474		}
475		key := makeCacheKey(core, resolved, normResource)
476		if hit, ok := m.cacheLookup(key); ok {
477			return hit, nil
478		}
479	
480		exchanged, err := m.runExchange(ctx, core, resolved)
481		if err != nil {
482			return "", err
483		}
484		m.cacheStore(key, exchanged)
485		return exchanged.AccessToken, nil
486	}
487	
488	// resolve fills empty TokenRequest fields with Config defaults.
489	func (m *Manager) resolve(req TokenRequest) TokenRequest {
490		if req.RequestedTokenType == "" {
491			req.RequestedTokenType = m.cfg.RequestedTokenType
492		}
493		if req.Scope == "" {
494			req.Scope = m.cfg.Scope
495		}
496		return req
497	}
498	
499	// coreTokenExpired reports whether the core token is not currently
500	// usable: either its `exp` claim is in the past (or within
501	// exchangeSkew of now) or its `nbf` claim is in the future. JWT
502	// parse failures (and tokens without an `exp` claim) are reported as
503	// not-expired so opaque access tokens flow through the rest of the
504	// resolution rules unchanged.
505	//
506	// Applying exchangeSkew here closes a race: a token expiring at
507	// now+1ms is technically "live", but if we present it to the resource
508	// (or STS), the request body's TLS handshake + DNS + queue can easily
509	// push the AS-side validation past the wire-side exp — landing a
510	// confusing invalid_grant / 401 that triggers a re-login at the worst
511	// moment. The cost is one fresh login slightly earlier than strictly
512	// necessary; the cache's exchangeSkew uses the same window so the
513	// two stay in sync.
514	//
515	// Enforcing `nbf` is defence in depth — a token that's not-yet-valid
516	// shouldn't be presented either. RFC 7519 §4.1.5 requires the
517	// processor to reject a JWT with `nbf` in the future.
518	func coreTokenExpired(coreJWT string, now time.Time) bool {
519		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(coreJWT)
520		if err != nil {
521			return false
522		}
523		if !claims.NotBefore.IsZero() && now.Before(claims.NotBefore) {
524			return true
525		}
526		if claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
527			return false
528		}
529		return !now.Add(exchangeSkew).Before(claims.ExpiresAt)
530	}
531	
532	// coreTokenAudienceIncludes reports whether the core JWT's `aud` claim
533	// covers target. target is expected to already be in normalised form;
534	// aud entries are normalised here so a trailing-slash / case difference
535	// between the AS and the caller doesn't force a needless STS exchange.
536	func coreTokenAudienceIncludes(coreJWT, target string) bool {
537		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(coreJWT)
538		if err != nil {
539			return false
540		}
541		for _, aud := range claims.Audience {
542			if oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL(aud) == target {
543				return true
544			}
545		}
546		return false
547	}
548	
549	// maxCachedTokenLifetime bounds entries with an unknown wire-side
550	// expiry. Today this can't happen on the exchange path (sts.Exchange
551	// rejects non-positive expires_in), but it would still apply if a
552	// future code path stored a TokenSet without ExpiresAt — capping at 1h
553	// prevents an indefinitely-cached stale token in that case.
554	const maxCachedTokenLifetime = time.Hour
555	
556	// cachedToken is one entry in the per-process exchange cache.
557	type cachedToken struct {
558		accessToken string
559		expiresAt   time.Time
560		cachedAt    time.Time
561	}
562	
563	func (c cachedToken) usable(now time.Time) bool {
564		if c.accessToken == "" {
565			return false
566		}
567		if c.expiresAt.IsZero() {
568			return now.Sub(c.cachedAt) < maxCachedTokenLifetime
569		}
570		return now.Add(exchangeSkew).Before(c.expiresAt)
571	}
572	
573	// cacheKey is a structurally-keyed exchange-cache key. Using a struct
574	// rather than a delimiter-joined string sidesteps any chance of two
575	// distinct (core token, resource, audience, requested-token-type,
576	// scope) tuples hashing to the same map slot via embedded delimiters
577	// in any field.
578	//
579	// CoreTokenHash is a SHA-256 of the core token rather than the token
580	// itself: a long-running embedder (daemon, server agent) accumulates
581	// one cache entry per (Resource, Audience, RequestedTokenType, Scope)
582	// tuple, so embedding the full token replicates the bearer N times
583	// across the per-process exchange cache. Memory dumps, crash reports,
584	// and profile heap snapshots then leak N copies. The hash is a stable
585	// identifier (collision-resistant for this purpose) that still
586	// distinguishes between cores from different logins.
587	type cacheKey struct {
588		CoreTokenHash      [sha256.Size]byte
589		Resource           string
590		Audience           string
591		RequestedTokenType string
592		Scope              string
593	}
594	
595	// makeCacheKey builds a cacheKey from the (resolved) request. Includes
596	// every wire-affecting field so different combinations don't shadow
597	// each other. normalizedResource is the caller-supplied Resource after
598	// normalisation, so https://api.example.com and
599	// https://api.example.com/ share a single cache entry.
600	func makeCacheKey(coreToken string, req TokenRequest, normalizedResource string) cacheKey {
601		return cacheKey{
602			CoreTokenHash:      sha256.Sum256([]byte(coreToken)),
603			Resource:           normalizedResource,
604			Audience:           req.Audience,
605			RequestedTokenType: req.RequestedTokenType,
606			Scope:              req.Scope,
607		}
608	}
609	
610	func (m *Manager) cacheLookup(key cacheKey) (string, bool) {
611		m.mu.Lock()
612		defer m.mu.Unlock()
613		entry, ok := m.cache[key]
614		if !ok {
615			return "", false
616		}
617		if !entry.usable(m.now()) {
618			delete(m.cache, key)
619			return "", false
620		}
621		return entry.accessToken, true
622	}
623	
624	func (m *Manager) cacheStore(key cacheKey, t *tokens.TokenSet) {
625		m.mu.Lock()
626		defer m.mu.Unlock()
627		m.cache[key] = cachedToken{
628			accessToken: t.AccessToken,
629			expiresAt:   t.ExpiresAt,
630			cachedAt:    m.now(),
631		}
632	}
633	
634	// fileLockPath adapts a derived lock path to ProcessLock via
635	// internal/proclock. The path field lets tests assert the per-identity
636	// derivation without importing proclock.
637	type fileLockPath struct {
638		path string
639		lock *proclock.FileLock
640	}
641	
642	func (f *fileLockPath) Acquire(ctx context.Context) (func(), error) {
643		return f.lock.Acquire(ctx) //nolint:wrapcheck // proclock already prefixes "proclock:"
644	}
645	
646	// processLock returns the test override if set, else the lazily-built
647	// default file lock. The lock path is keyed on (ClientID, Issuer) — the
648	// identity that scopes the stored credential — so unrelated CLIs sharing
649	// an issuer don't serialise against each other.
650	func (m *Manager) processLock() ProcessLock {
651		if p := m.lockOverride.Load(); p != nil {
652			return *p
653		}
654		m.lockOnce.Do(func() {
655			dir := m.cfg.LockDir
656			if dir == "" {
657				if cache, err := os.UserCacheDir(); err == nil {
658					dir = filepath.Join(cache, "auth-go")
659				} else {
660					dir = filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), "auth-go")
661				}
662			}
663			sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(m.cfg.ClientID + "\x00" + m.cfg.Issuer))
664			path := filepath.Join(dir, hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])+".lock")
665			m.defaultLock = &fileLockPath{path: path, lock: proclock.New(path)}
666		})
667		return m.defaultLock
668	}
669	
670	// runRefresh dispatches to the test override (if set) else a freshly built
671	// refresh.Client pointing at Issuer + RefreshPath. client_id is sent on
672	// both surfaces (Basic auth via the typed field, form body via Extra),
673	// matching runExchange — see sts.ExchangeRequest.ClientID for the why.
674	func (m *Manager) runRefresh(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
675		req := refresh.Request{
676			RefreshToken: refreshToken,
677			ClientID:     m.cfg.ClientID,
678			Extra:        url.Values{"client_id": {m.cfg.ClientID}},
679		}
680		if p := m.refreshOverride.Load(); p != nil {
681			return (*p)(ctx, req)
682		}
683		if strings.TrimSpace(m.cfg.RefreshPath) == "" {
684			return nil, ErrNoRefreshPath
685		}
686		client := &refresh.Client{
687			Transport:         m.cfg.Transport,
688			BaseURL:           m.cfg.Issuer,
689			Path:              m.cfg.RefreshPath,
690			UserAgent:         m.cfg.UserAgent,
691			AllowInsecureHTTP: m.cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP,
692		}
693		return client.Refresh(ctx, req) //nolint:wrapcheck // refresh.Refresh already prefixes "refresh token:"
694	}
695	
696	// loadTokenSet reads the full stored TokenSet for the configured issuer.
697	// ok=false (with nil error) means no credential is stored; a non-nil error
698	// is a genuine store failure (never collapsed to "not logged in").
699	func (m *Manager) loadTokenSet() (set tokens.TokenSet, ok bool, err error) {
700		t, err := m.cfg.Store.LoadTokens(m.cfg.Issuer)
701		if errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) {
702			return tokens.TokenSet{}, false, nil
703		}
704		if err != nil {
705			return tokens.TokenSet{}, false, fmt.Errorf("load core token: %w", err)
706		}
707		return t, true, nil
708	}
709	
710	// doRefresh runs the refresh_token grant for the currently stored refresh
711	// token and persists the rotated result. Assumes the caller holds both the
712	// in-process mutex and the cross-process lock and has already confirmed the
713	// stored login JWT is expired with a refresh token present.
714	//
715	// On invalid_grant it re-reads the store: if the refresh token changed
716	// (a non-cooperating actor rotated it under us) it retries once with the
717	// new token; otherwise the family is genuinely dead → ErrReauthRequired.
718	// Transport and other errors are returned as-is, never as reauth, and
719	// never delete the stored credential.
720	func (m *Manager) doRefresh(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
721		set, ok, err := m.loadTokenSet()
722		if err != nil {
723			return "", err
724		}
725		if !ok || !set.HasRefresh() {
726			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
727		}
728		sent := set.RefreshToken
729	
730		res, err := m.runRefresh(ctx, sent)
731		if err == nil {
732			if perr := m.persistRefreshed(set, res); perr != nil {
733				return "", perr
734			}
735			return res.AccessToken, nil
736		}
737		if !errors.Is(err, refresh.ErrInvalidGrant) {
738			return "", err
739		}
740	
741		// Rotation-race recovery: another actor may have rotated the refresh
742		// token between our read and our grant. Re-read; retry once if so.
743		cur, ok, rerr := m.loadTokenSet()
744		if rerr != nil {
745			return "", rerr
746		}
747		if !ok {
748			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn // credential deleted concurrently (e.g. logout)
749		}
750		if !cur.HasRefresh() {
751			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn // refresh token cleared concurrently
752		}
753		if cur.RefreshToken != sent {
754			// A non-cooperating actor rotated the RT under us; retry once.
755			res, err = m.runRefresh(ctx, cur.RefreshToken)
756			if err == nil {
757				if perr := m.persistRefreshed(cur, res); perr != nil {
758					return "", perr
759				}
760				return res.AccessToken, nil
761			}
762			if !errors.Is(err, refresh.ErrInvalidGrant) {
763				return "", err
764			}
765		}
766		return "", ErrReauthRequired
767	}
768	
769	// persistRefreshed merges the grant response onto the prior set and saves
770	// it. A non-rotating server (empty refresh_token / scope in the response)
771	// must not wipe a still-valid refresh token, so empty fields fall back to
772	// the prior values. The new login JWT and ExpiresAt always replace.
773	// SaveCoreToken clears the in-process exchange cache as a side effect, so
774	// the next Token() re-exchanges against the new login JWT.
775	func (m *Manager) persistRefreshed(prev tokens.TokenSet, res *tokens.TokenSet) error {
776		merged := *res
777		if merged.RefreshToken == "" {
778			merged.RefreshToken = prev.RefreshToken
779		}
780		if merged.Scope == "" {
781			merged.Scope = prev.Scope
782		}
783		if merged.TokenType == "" {
784			merged.TokenType = prev.TokenType
785		}
786		// saveCoreTokenLocked (NOT SaveCoreToken) — persistRefreshed runs from
787		// inside refreshLocked, which already holds refreshMu + processLock.
788		// Re-entering them here would self-deadlock.
789		if err := m.saveCoreTokenLocked(merged); err != nil {
790			return fmt.Errorf("refresh: persist: %w", err)
791		}
792		return nil
793	}
794	
795	// ensureFreshLogin returns a usable login JWT, transparently re-minting an
796	// expired one from the stored refresh token. The fast path takes no locks:
797	// a still-fresh token (the common case) returns immediately. ErrNotLoggedIn
798	// when no credential is stored or an expired one has no refresh token;
799	// ErrReauthRequired when the refresh token is revoked/expired.
800	// The fast path intentionally mirrors freshOrProceed's checks to avoid
801	// taking refreshMu on the common case of a still-fresh token; keep the two
802	// in sync if you add an early-exit condition.
803	func (m *Manager) ensureFreshLogin(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
804		set, ok, err := m.loadTokenSet()
805		if err != nil {
806			return "", err
807		}
808		if !ok {
809			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
810		}
811		// A usable token must be non-empty as well as unexpired. A BYO Store
812		// that returns a TokenSet with an empty AccessToken (without
813		// ErrNotFound) must not yield an empty bearer — coreTokenExpired("")
814		// reports not-expired (parse failure), so guard the empty case here.
815		if set.AccessToken != "" && !coreTokenExpired(set.AccessToken, m.now()) {
816			return set.AccessToken, nil
817		}
818		if !set.HasRefresh() {
819			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
820		}
821		return m.refreshLocked(ctx)
822	}
823	
824	// refreshLocked performs the serialize-and-double-check re-mint: the
825	// in-process mutex coalesces goroutines, the cross-process lock coalesces
826	// processes, and a store re-read after each gate lets a late waiter return
827	// the token a peer just minted instead of re-minting.
828	func (m *Manager) refreshLocked(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
829		m.refreshMu.Lock()
830		defer m.refreshMu.Unlock()
831	
832		if tok, done, err := m.freshOrProceed(); done {
833			return tok, err
834		}
835	
836		release, err := m.processLock().Acquire(ctx)
837		if err != nil {
838			return "", fmt.Errorf("refresh: acquire lock: %w", err)
839		}
840		defer release()
841	
842		if tok, done, err := m.freshOrProceed(); done {
843			return tok, err
844		}
845	
846		return m.doRefresh(ctx)
847	}
848	
849	// freshOrProceed re-reads the store and reports whether the caller has a
850	// terminal result. done=true means return (tok, err) directly — the token
851	// is fresh now, no credential exists, or an expired token has no refresh
852	// token. done=false means "still expired with a refresh token — proceed to
853	// the re-mint".
854	func (m *Manager) freshOrProceed() (string, bool, error) {
855		set, ok, err := m.loadTokenSet()
856		if err != nil {
857			return "", true, err
858		}
859		if !ok {
860			return "", true, ErrNotLoggedIn
861		}
862		if set.AccessToken != "" && !coreTokenExpired(set.AccessToken, m.now()) {
863			return set.AccessToken, true, nil
864		}
865		if !set.HasRefresh() {
866			return "", true, ErrNotLoggedIn
867		}
868		return "", false, nil
869	}
870	
871	// runExchange dispatches to either Config.Exchange (test override) or
872	// a freshly built sts.Client pointing at m.cfg.Issuer + m.cfg.STSPath.
873	func (m *Manager) runExchange(ctx context.Context, coreToken string, req TokenRequest) (*tokens.TokenSet, error) {
874		stsReq := sts.ExchangeRequest{
875			SubjectToken:       coreToken,
876			SubjectTokenType:   m.cfg.SubjectTokenType,
877			RequestedTokenType: req.RequestedTokenType,
878			Audience:           req.Audience,
879			Resource:           req.Resource,
880			Scope:              req.Scope,
881			// Public-client identification per RFC 6749 §3.2.1 (public
882			// clients SHOULD include client_id on requests; we go further
883			// and ALWAYS include it). Sent on both surfaces simultaneously:
884			//   - ClientID populates HTTP Basic Auth — required by servers
885			//     that read credentials only from the Basic header on the
886			//     token-exchange grant (zitadel-based servers as of
887			//     2026-05 are a known example: pkg/op/token_exchange.go
888			//     reads only from r.BasicAuth()).
889			//   - Extra["client_id"] populates the form body — required by
890			//     servers that read credentials from the form, plus it's
891			//     the §2.3.1 form for confidential clients.
892			// DO NOT delete either line independently. The two surfaces
893			// target different server implementations; the test server
894			// validates both, so passing tests do not prove production
895			// safety against arbitrary auth servers. m.cfg.ClientID is
896			// non-empty by Config.validate, so the resulting request has
897			// at least one credential surface populated.
898			ClientID: m.cfg.ClientID,
899			Extra:    url.Values{"client_id": {m.cfg.ClientID}},
900		}
901	
902		if p := m.exchangeOverride.Load(); p != nil {
903			return (*p)(ctx, stsReq)
904		}
905	
906		if strings.TrimSpace(m.cfg.STSPath) == "" {
907			return nil, ErrNoSTSPath
908		}
909	
910		stsClient := &sts.Client{
911			Transport:         m.cfg.Transport,
912			BaseURL:           m.cfg.Issuer,
913			Path:              m.cfg.STSPath,
914			UserAgent:         m.cfg.UserAgent,
915			AllowInsecureHTTP: m.cfg.AllowInsecureHTTP,
916		}
917		return stsClient.Exchange(ctx, stsReq) //nolint:wrapcheck // sts.Exchange already prefixes "token exchange:"
918	}
